Rashi on Zevachim 4a:18:1.english: Zevah Todat Shelamav - meaning, its slaughter should be for the sake of a thanks offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:2.english: Fit - and it fulfilled the obligation of the owner.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:3.english: Unfit - meaning, it did not fulfill the obligation of the owner.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:19:4.english: A thanks offering is called a peace offering - as it is written: 'his thanks offering of peace offerings,' just like 'the sin offering of the congregation' (Leviticus 4:21) and 'the Torah of Moses My servant' (Malachi 3:22).

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:20:1.english: Anan mi'zevah todah ka'amarinan - Our derivation, while Abba Ḥanin's is from 'his thanks offering of peace offerings'.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:21:1.english: From where is a sin offering and a guilt offering derived? - In the Torat Kohanim, it is taught regarding this verse: 'and the meat of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering... on the day of his offering it shall be eaten,' we learn concerning a thanks offering that it is eaten for a day and a night.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:21:2.english: From where is a sin offering and a guilt offering derived? - The verse states 'zevaḥ'.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:25:1.english: You did not differentiate - because all of them were included above.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:26:1.english: As its disqualification concerns the offering itself - It explains this further on.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:26:2.english: And it applies to the four sacrificial rites - for if one slaughtered not for its sake, or collected, conveyed, or sprinkled not for its sake, even if he intended only for the slaughter to be not for its sake, it is disqualified, as we derived above. But a change of owner is relevant only to the sprinkling, for when we derived that slaughter disqualifies due to a change of owner, it means if he slaughtered with the intention of sprinkling the blood for another's atonement. But if he slaughtered not for the sake of the owner and did not mention sprinkling the blood, this is not considered an intention, as a change of owner is relevant to an offering only for atonement, and atonement is through sprinkling. And this is what we say later in this chapter (Zevachim 10a): if one said, 'I am hereby slaughtering for so-and-so,' it is fit. If he slaughtered it with the intention of sprinkling the blood for so-and-so, it is unfit. And similarly for collection and conveying, a change of owner is not relevant unless he intended to collect with the intention of sprinkling for another.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:27:1.english: And it applies after death - But a change of owners is not relevant after death. In Pesachim (61a) our Rabbi raised a difficulty: perhaps since the obligation is not from the Torah, so too there is no change of offering after death, for what practical difference is there that they did not fulfill the obligation, for the heirs are not obligated to bring another? For there is a dispute in Kiddushin (13b) regarding a woman who brought her sin offering and died, the heirs should bring her burnt offering. Shmuel said that this is only if she designated it during her lifetime, and Rav Ashi said even if she did not designate it during her lifetime. Here, one should say, according to the one who holds that obligation is not from the Torah, that there is no change of offering after death. At least two of these arguments are precise. It can be said that the practical difference is if he designated two peace offerings or two burnt offerings conditionally, and specified that if one dies or is lost, the second should be brought as a burnt offering, like the first. And if the first was brought properly, the second would be non-sacred. But when the owners died and the heir sacrificed one not for its sake, it is as if it was lost, and the second is sacrificed in its place. And if the first was brought properly, then the second is non-sacred. But if he did not specify anything, but simply designated two conditionally, then even if the first was brought properly, the second grazes and its value is brought as a burnt offering, as is found later (Zevachim 11a) regarding the remainder of a sin offering, which is brought as a burnt offering. And it can also be said that after death there is a prohibition in changing the offering when one changes it, but there is no prohibition in changing the owner since there is no owner. However, he still did not know the derivation of "that which has gone out of your lips" from which the prohibition of changing the offering is derived, as it is brought later.

Rashi on Zevachim 4a:27:2.english: And it applies to communal offerings - This is not the case with a change of owners, for if one slaughtered the daily offering for its sake, he is its owner. And even if [he slaughtered it] for the sake of an idol worshiper, it is not disqualified, for we require that the other person be similar to him, obligated in atonement like him. Blessed [is God].

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:11:1.hebrew: יעשה כלל - שיהו כל עשיותיו לשם שלמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:11:1.english: "Shall offer" is a generalization - [Meaning,] that all of its acts [of service] must be for the sake of a peace offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:11:2.hebrew: זבח פרט - שחיטה הוא דבעי לשמה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:11:2.english: “A sacrifice” is a detail - It is slaughter that requires [to be done] for its own sake:

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:12:1.hebrew: אי כתיב יעשה שלמים זבח כדקאמרת - דמשמע כללא, שיהו עשייתו שלמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:12:1.english: If it were written, “he shall offer peace offerings, a sacrifice,” as you say - For it would imply a generalization, [namely] that its offering should be [as] peace offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:12:2.hebrew: השתא דכתיב יעשה זבח שלמים - לא גמר הכלל את דבריו, ולא נשלם להשמיענו על מה הוזכרו כאן העשיות, עד שבא "זבח" והפסיק את הדבר:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:12:2.english: Now that it is written: "Shall offer a sacrifice of peace offerings" - The generalization did not complete its statement, and it was not finished informing us about what the "offerings" mentioned here refer to, until "sacrifice" came and interrupted the matter.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:12:3.hebrew: כלל שאינו מלא - ולא נתמלא דבריו, כלומר להשלים את הכלל מלא, פרדאשביי"ן בלע"ז:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:12:3.english: An incomplete generalization - Its statement was not completed, [meaning] it is not fully complete — pardashbeiyin in Old French.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:1.hebrew: עשייתו - עבודות המיוחדות: שחיטה, וזריקה, קבלה, והולכה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:1.english: Its performance - The specific sacrificial services: slaughtering, sprinkling, receiving [the blood], and conveying [it].

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:2.hebrew: לה' - כלומר, יעשה זבח שלמים לה':
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:2.english: Unto the Lord - The peace-offering sacrifice shall be made unto the Lord.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:3.hebrew: שפיכת שירים - שנשפכין שירי הדם ליסוד, והוא [אחר] שנתן ארבע מתנות, ואינן מעכבין כפרה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:3.english: Pouring the remains - That the remains of the blood are poured onto the base [of the altar] after he has applied the four applications, and they do not impede atonement.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:4.hebrew: הא תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל כו' - בשילהי פרק אלו טריפות (חולין דף סו.), גבי פרשת חגבים:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:14:4.english: This the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught, etc. - At the end of [the chapter] Eilu Terefot (Chullin 66a), regarding the passage about locusts.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:16:1.hebrew: איכא למימר הכי - אף כל עבודה וחייבין עליה בחוץ, ואתיא לה זריקה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:16:1.english: One can say this - [Just as the detail is] a rite for which one is liable when performed outside, [so too any] rite for which one is liable outside, and sprinkling comes in under this [category].

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:16:2.hebrew: ואיכא למימר הכי - עבודה שטעונה צפון, ואתיא לה קבלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:16:2.english: And it is possible to say so - [Namely, any] service that requires [performance in the] north, and [thus] collection [of the blood] comes in as well.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:18:1.hebrew: שקולין הן - המדות שוות, והי מינייהו מפקת? אי דרשת הא, אנא דרישנא לאידך. הלכך יבאו שניהם, והולכה על כרחך לא תפקה מכלל קבלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:18:1.english: They are equal - The [hermeneutical] principles are equal, and which of them would you exclude? If you expound this one, I will expound the other. Therefore, both of them are included, and you cannot, of necessity, exclude conveying [the blood to the altar] from the category of receiving [the blood].

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:19:1.hebrew: מדרב אשי - מונרצה לו לכפר, וכלל ופרט לאיתויי קבלה, דאי לזריקה לא איצטריך:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:19:1.english: From Rav Ashi - [Sprinkling is derived] from "and it shall be accepted for him to atone." And [the verse about the ram, which is] a general statement followed by a specific one, comes to include collection [of the blood], for if it were [meant] for sprinkling, it would not be needed.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:1:1.hebrew: ואע"ג דתרתי לאו דוקא תרתי דוקא - אע"ג דמותבינן ארבעה פרכי, איכא תרתי שאינן עיקר, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:1:1.english: And although two are not precise, two are precise - Although we raise four refutations, there are two that are not essential, as [the Gemara] explains as it proceeds.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:1:2.hebrew: תרתי מיהא דוקא - הגמרא והשתא מפרש אמאי תרתי לאו דוקא:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:1:2.english: Two are in any event precise - And now [the Gemara] explains why two are not precise.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:21:1.hebrew: שכן יש עמו דמים אחרים - שבאין עמו חטאת ועולה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:21:1.english: Since there is other blood with it - For a sin offering and a burnt offering come with it.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:23:1.hebrew: אשכחן שלמים - בין בשינוי קודש, בין בשינוי בעלים:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:23:1.english: We have found [a source for] peace offerings - Both for a change of sanctity and for a change of owners.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:24:1.hebrew: שכן טעונין כו' - ושאר זבחים, יש מהן שאין טעונים סמיכה ולא נסכים, כגון בכור ומעשר ופסח; ויש מהן שאין טעונין נסכים, כגון חטאת ואשם; ובכולן אין אחד שיהא טעון חזה ושוק:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:24:1.english: For it requires, etc. - And of the other offerings, there are some that require neither placing of hands nor libations, such as the firstborn, the tithe [of animals], and the Paschal offering; and there are some that do not require libations, such as the sin offering and the guilt offering; and among all of them, there is not one that requires the breast and the hind leg.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:26:1.hebrew: ליפסלו - שהרי לא נעשו כהלכתן, ואין זריקתן מתרת בשרן לאכילה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:26:1.english: Let them be disqualified - For they were not performed according to their proper law, and their sprinkling does not render their flesh permitted for eating.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:28:1.hebrew: ואיצטריך - למיכתב "זאת התורה", למיגמר משלמים. ולא תימא: ממוצא שפתיך נפקא, דלכתחילה בעינן לשמה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:28:1.english: And it was necessary - to write "This is the law," in order to derive [the law] from the peace-offerings. And do not say: it is derived from "that which has gone out of your lips," [which would teach] that at the outset we require [that the offering be brought] for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:3:1.hebrew: ולרב פנחס כו' - ולקמן בשילהי שמעתין אזלה לה הך פירכא דלאחר מיתה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:3:1.english: And according to Rav Pineḥas, etc. - And below, at the end of this passage, this refutation concerning [the case of] after death falls away.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:5:1.hebrew: לכפר עליו - היינו זריקה. אלמא, זריקה לשם בעלים בעיא:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:5:1.english: To atone for him - This refers to the throwing [of the blood]. Evidently, the throwing requires [being done] for the sake of the owners.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:5:2.hebrew: את שעליו - כגון נדר, דאמר: הרי עלי עולה, חייב באחריותו. אם הפריש בהמה לנדרו, אם מתה או נגנבה — דהכי משמע: אותו שעליו, יקריב אותו, ״ונרצה לו״; ועד שיקריבנו לא נרצה ולא נפטר:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:5:2.english: That which is upon him - For example, a vow, where he said, "It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering": he bears responsibility for it. If he set aside an animal for his vow and it died or was stolen [he must bring another], for this is what [the verse] means: that which is incumbent upon him, he shall offer it, "and it shall be accepted for him"; but until he offers it, it is not accepted and he is not discharged.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:5:3.hebrew: את שאינו עליו - כגון דאמר הרי זו עולה:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:5:3.english: And that which is not upon him - For example, where he said, "Behold, this is a burnt offering."

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:7:1.hebrew: מונרצה לו לכפר קאמר - דהכי משמע ״ונרצה״ לו, לכפר עליו ולא לחבירו:
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:7:1.english: He is saying "and it shall be accepted for him, to atone" - For this is what it implies: [it is accepted] for him, to atone for him, and not for another.

Rashi on Zevachim 4b:9:1.hebrew: שכן עבודה שחייבין עליה בחוץ - דכתיב (ויקרא י״ז:ג׳) אשר ישחט מחוץ למחנה. וזורק נמי מרבינן ליה לקמן בפ' השוחט (זבחים דף קז.) "דם שפך", לרבות הזורק. תאמר בקבלה והולכה שאין חייבין עליה בחוץ, דתנן בפ' בתרא (שם קיב:) "והיוצק והבולל כו' והמקבל דמים בחוץ פטור":
Rashi on Zevachim 4b:9:1.english: Since it is a rite for which one is liable if performed outside - As it is written (Leviticus 17:3): "Who slaughters [an ox... ] outside the camp." And sprinkling too we include later, in the chapter Hashochet (Zevachim 107a), [from the verse] "he spilled blood," to include one who sprinkles. Would you say this about collection and conveyance, for which one is not liable if performed outside? For we learned in the last chapter (ibid. 112b): "And one who pours, and one who mixes, etc., and one who collects blood outside is exempt."

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 4b:24.english: All offerings brought to the Temple by an individual, with the exceptions of the firstborn of a kosher animal, a Paschal offering, and an animal tithe, require the person bringing the offering to perform the rite of laying hands. This is accomplished by pressing down with all one’s strength both of one’s hands between the horns on the head of the animal to be sacrificed, before it is slaughtered. No communal offerings require this rite except the bull brought for an unwitting communal sin and the scapegoat on Yom Kippur. When performing this ritual for a sin offering, a guilt offering, or a voluntary burnt offering, the person bringing the offering also recites a confessional prayer. An offering requiring laying hands is not invalidated if this ceremony is not performed. Women are not obligated to perform the rite of laying hands. According to some opinions, they may perform a ritual approximating it if they so desire.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 4b:26.hebrew: שאלו בתוס': הרי בדיני קדשים יש צד מיוחד, שבשאר דינים כל שלא נעשה כראוי — אין זו מצוה. אבל בקדשים אנו אומרים שכדי לפסול את הקודש (על ידי מעשה או הימנעות ממעשה) יש צורך שיהא זה דבר ש"שנה עליו הכתוב לעכב" כלומר, שהלכה זו נאמרה פעמיים, פעם אחת לעשות כן לכתחילה, ופעם אחרת שאם לא עשה — הרי זה מעכב ופוסל לגמרי. ואם כן, היכן מצינו בשינוי קודש כתוב שני לעכב? ותירצו כי לעיל היו כמה כתובים שמלשונם יש ללמוד שמדברים בשינוי קודש, אלא שאמרנו שכיון שלא נצרכו לגופם — תנם ענין לדבר אחר. ומעתה זו היא השאלה: מפני מה לא למדו משני הכתובים המדברים בשינוי קודש שיש בכך "שנה הכתוב לעכב".
Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 4b:26.english: The Tosafot asked: In the laws of consecrated items there is a unique aspect, that in other laws, whatever is not done properly is not a mitzva. But regarding consecrated items we say that in order to disqualify a consecrated item (through an action or abstention from an action), it is necessary for it to be something about which 'the verse repeated to make it indispensable.' That is to say, this halakha was stated twice, once to do it *ab initio*, and another time that if one did not do it, it is indispensable and completely disqualifies. If so, where do we find in deviation from the type of offering a second verse to make it indispensable? And they answered that above there were several verses from whose language it can be learned that they speak of deviation from the type of offering, but we said that since they were not needed for their own sake, apply them to another matter. And now this is the question: Why did they not learn from the two verses that speak of deviation from the type of offering that there is here 'the verse repeated to make it indispensable'?

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:27:1.english: And it applies after death - But a change of owners is not relevant after death. In Pesachim (61a) our Rabbi raised a difficulty: perhaps since the obligation is not from the Torah, so too there is no change of offering after death, for what practical difference is there that they did not fulfill the obligation, for the heirs are not obligated to bring another? For there is a dispute in Kiddushin (13b) regarding a woman who brought her sin offering and died, the heirs should bring her burnt offering. Shmuel said that this is only if she designated it during her lifetime, and Rav Ashi said even if she did not designate it during her lifetime. Here, one should say, according to the one who holds that obligation is not from the Torah, that there is no change of offering after death, so at least two things are precise. It can be said that the practical difference is if he designated two peace offerings or two burnt offerings conditionally, and specified that if one dies or is lost, the second should be brought as a burnt offering, like the first. And if the first was brought properly, the second would be non-sacred. But when the owners died and the heir sacrificed one not for its sake, it is as if it was lost, and the second is sacrificed in its place. And if the first was brought properly, then the second is non-sacred. But if he did not specify anything, but simply designated two conditionally, then even if the first was brought properly, the second grazes and its value is brought as a burnt offering, as is found later (Zevachim 11a) regarding the remainder of a sin offering, which is brought as a burnt offering. And it can also be said that after death there is a prohibition in changing the offering when one changes it, but there is no prohibition in changing the owner since there is no owner. However, he still did not know the derivation of "that which has gone out of your lips" from which the prohibition of changing the offering is derived, as it is brought later.

Tosafot on Zevachim 4a:27:2.english: And it applies to communal offerings - This is not the case with a change of owners, for if one slaughtered the daily offering for its sake, he is its owner. And even if [he slaughtered it] for the sake of an idol worshiper, it is not disqualified, for we require that the other person be similar to him, obligated in atonement like him. Blessed [is God].

Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:18:1.hebrew: שקולים הם ויבאו שניהם - אע"ג דהכא תרתי והכא חדא, חשיב להו שקולין. והקשה הרב רבי חיים, דהשתא משמע דהיכא דלא ידע הי מינייהו לרבויי, מרבי תרוייהו. וכן בריש ב"ק (דף ג.) דמרבי מושלח שן ורגל משום דשקולין הן, וכן בפ"ק דערכין (דף ד:) גבי נפשות. ואילו בפרק כל האסורים (תמורה דף כח:) ופרק שור שנגח ארבעה וה' (ב"ק דף מ:) דרשינן "מן הבהמה" להוציא את הרובע, "ומן הצאן" להוציא את הנוגח, וקאמר: מפני שיש ברובע מה שאין בנוגח, ויש בנוגח מה שאין ברובע, הוצרך לומר רובע והוצרך לומר נוגח. ותירץ, דהיכא דאיכא משמעות בריבוי, מרבינן כל השקולים, כי הכא דזבח משמע לרבויי כעין זביחה כל שהיא עבודה. וכן "ושלח" יש במשמע רגל ושן, ונפשות נמי משמע הכל. אבל "מן" לא משמע למעוטי שניהם:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:18:1.english: "They are equal, and both are included" - Even though here there are two [possibilities] and there only one, [the Gemara] considers them equal. And the Rav, Rabbi Chaim, raised a difficulty: For now it implies that where one does not know which of them to include, we include both. And so too at the beginning of Bava Kamma (3a), where it includes [the damage of] "shen" and "regel" from "mishalei'ach," because they are equal; and so too in the first chapter of Arakhin (4b) regarding [the valuations of] persons. Yet in the chapter Kol HaAsurin (Temurah 28b) and the chapter Shor SheNagach Arba'a VaChamisha (Bava Kamma 40b), we expound "from the animals" to exclude one who had relations with a person [i.e., the rovea], and "and from the flock" to exclude the goring ox, and [the Gemara] says: Because the rovea has something the gorer lacks, and the gorer has something the rovea lacks, it was necessary to state [the case of] rovea and it was necessary to state [the case of] the gorer. And [Rabbi Chaim] answered that where the wording allows for an inclusion, we include all equal [possibilities]. So here, the word "sacrifice" implies including anything similar to slaughtering, which is any [Temple] service. And likewise, "mishalei'ach" implies both "regel" and "shen," and "persons" too implies everything. But the word "min" (from) does not imply excluding both:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:26:1.hebrew: אימא היכא דשחיט שלא לשמן ליפסלו - תימה: הא בכל דוכתא בעינן בקדשים ש[שינה] לעכב, והכא לא שינה? וי"ל דפריך משינוי קודש, דאיכא תרי קראי, ואמרי' לעיל: אם אינו ענין לשינוי קודש, תנהו ענין לשינוי בעלים. ופריך דהשתא: אימר תרוייהו בשינוי קודש ולעכב? וקשה, מאי משני "אמר קרא מוצא שפתיך"? דלמא ההוא קרא אתא לשינוי בעלים, דלא אשכחן ששינה בהן הכתוב! ולא קשה מידי, דמוצא שפתיך לא משמע שינוי בעלים. [הג"ה] ונראה דפריך מכח סברא, כעין קושיא דר"ל דלקמיה: דאימא דליפסלו, כיון דאמרת דלא עלו לשם חובה? או נימא דיעלו, דאם כשרין הן ירצו, ואם אין מרצין למה באין? [ומיהו] לא דמי, דריש לקיש פריך: יהו כשרין גמורין כמו שאר קדשים דלא שנה לעכב בו, ליפסלו? והכא לא הוה ליה למיפרך "שלא לשמה ליפסלו", אלא הוה ליה למימר: "וליתכשרו ויעלו לחובה כשאר קדשים שלא שנה לעכב", כל כמה דאכתי לא ידע קרא דמוצא שפתיך. ואי פריך "ליפסלו" דנגמר מחטאת [ופסח] בהיקישא דזאת התורה כדפרישית בסמוך, אי "במה מצינו" איכא למיפרך, שכן כרת. וא' בהקישא דזאת התורה, א"כ ליכתוב חדא, או לחטאת גרידא או פסח גרידא. ואי נאמר דבכל דוכתא דמצרכינן שנה לעכב היינו מהכא [מדכתיב] מוצא שפתיך וגו', א"כ אתי שפיר הא דפריך "וליפסלו" כו'. ע"כ הג"ה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:26:1.english: "Say that where he slaughtered them not for their sake, they should be disqualified" - This is puzzling: Everywhere regarding sacrificial offerings we require that [Scripture] state a change [as] invalidating, and here it did not state a change [as invalidating]? And one can answer that [the Gemara] is asking from a change of sanctity, where there are two verses, and we said earlier: If it is not relevant to a change of sanctity, apply it to a change of owners. And [the Gemara] asks: Now, say that both [verses] are about a change of sanctity and [are meant] to invalidate? And this is difficult: What does [the Gemara] answer, "Scripture says: 'That which comes out of your lips'"? Perhaps that verse comes for a change of owners, for we do not find that Scripture changed [the law] regarding them! But this is not difficult at all, since "that which comes out of your lips" does not imply a change of owners. [Gloss:] And it appears that [the Gemara] asks from reasoning, similar to Reish Lakish's question later: Say that they should be disqualified, since you said that they did not ascend for the sake of an obligation? Or let us say that they do ascend, for if they are fit they bring favor, and if they do not bring favor, why do they come? [But nevertheless] it is not comparable, for Reish Lakish asks: Should they be fully fit like other offerings, regarding which [Scripture] did not make a change invalidating, [rather than] be disqualified? But here [the Gemara] should not have asked "not for their sake, let them be disqualified," but should have said: "And let them be fit and ascend for the sake of an obligation, like other offerings regarding which [Scripture] did not make a change invalidating," so long as it did not yet know the verse "that which comes out of your lips." And if [the Gemara] asks "let them be disqualified," [on the basis] that it is derived from the sin offering [and Passover offering] by the juxtaposition of "this is the law," as I explained shortly above — if so, a "what do we find" argument can be refuted, since [those] carry [the penalty of] karet. And one [verse is needed] for the juxtaposition of "this is the law"; if so, [Scripture] should have written one, either for the sin offering alone or the Passover offering alone. And if we say that everywhere we require that a change be invalidating, it is from here, [as] it is written "that which comes out of your lips," etc., then what the Gemara asks, "let them be disqualified," is well understood, etc. End of gloss:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:2:1.hebrew: מחשבה בעלמא - ואפי' יהא צריך דיבור, כיון דליכא מעשה הוי כמחשבה בעלמא. ויש תימה: דהכא משוי להו, ובפ' תמיד נשחט (פסחים סב:) משמע שיש חילוק, דמפרש מה בין לשמן לשלא לשמן, לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו: זה פסולו בגופו וזה אין פסולו בגופו. וי"ל דכיון דלא מיפסיל אלא מפני שאין יכול לאכול כזית, כגון לשם חולה וזקן, חשיב טפי פסולו בקודש מחמת דבר אחר, כיון דאם היה יכול לאכול היה כשר. וקשה, דעל כרחין שלא למנוין ולערלים ולטמאין צריך לומר דלא חשיבי פסולן בגופו, כי היכי דלא תיקשי לן נמי: מה בין לשמן ושלא לשמן, למנוין ושלא למנוין, למולין ולערלים, לטמאין ולטהורים? וי"ל דשינוי בעלים חשבינן פסולו בגופו, משום דתלוי בזריקה (בכפרה) ושם בעלים [על הכפרה]; אבל שלא לאוכלין ושלא למנויין תלוי בשחיטה, ואין שם בעלים על השחיטה. אי נמי, שלא לאוכלין [ושלא למנויין] יכול לקיים מחשבתו בהיתר [באותן] שיהיו מנויין עליו, אם אינם חולים וזקנים; אבל שלא לשמה אינו יכול לקיימו, לכך קרוי פסולו בגופו:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:2:1.english: Mere thought - Even if it requires speech, since there is no act, it is like mere thought. And there is a difficulty: here [the Gemara] equates them, but in the chapter Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 62b) it implies that there is a distinction, as it explains "What is the difference between [slaughtering] for their sake and not for their sake, [or] for those who will eat it and not for those who will eat it?": this one's disqualification is in the body [of the offering], and that one's disqualification is not in the body. And one can say that since it is disqualified only because [the designated people] cannot eat an olive-bulk, such as [if it was slaughtered] for the sake of a sick person or an elderly person, its disqualification is considered more to be [one] in the sacred [offering] due to something else, since if he had been able to eat, it would have been valid. But this is difficult, for [in the case of slaughtering] not for those counted [on it], and for the uncircumcised and the impure, we must necessarily say that their disqualification is not considered to be in the body, so that it will not also pose a difficulty for us: What is the difference between [slaughtering] for their sake and not for their sake, for those counted and not for those counted, for the circumcised and the uncircumcised, for the impure and the pure? And one can say that we consider deviation with regard to the owners to be a disqualification in the body, because it depends on the throwing [of the blood] (for atonement), and there the owners' name is on the atonement; but [slaughtering] not for those who will eat and not for those counted depends on the slaughter, and the owners' name is not on the slaughter. Alternatively, [in the case of] not for those who will eat [and not for those counted], he can fulfill his intention permissibly, [by having] those [people] counted on it, if they are not sick or elderly; but [in the case of] not for its sake, he cannot fulfill it, and therefore it is called a disqualification in the body.

Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:6:1.hebrew: הגה"ה - ה"ג במגילה (דף ח.): "מאי משמעות [משמע]?" אמר רב יצחק בר אבדימי:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:6:1.english: Gloss: So is the text in Megillah (8a): "What is [the proof]?" Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:7:1.hebrew: רב אשי (אמר) מונרצה לו קאמר - תימה: למה לי קרא לשינוי בעלים בזריקה? הא אפי' שאר עבודות לא מיפסלי אלא בשוחט על מנת לזרוק, כ"ש זורק עצמו [דבעינן] שם בעלים:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:7:1.english: Rav Ashi (said) he is speaking of "and it shall be accepted for him" - It is astonishing: why do I need a verse for a change of owner in the sprinkling? Even the other services are disqualified only in the case of one who slaughters with the intent to sprinkle [for a different owner]; all the more so one who sprinkles himself, [for whom] the name of the owner is required:

Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:9:1.hebrew: שכן עבודה וחייבים - פירוש: עבודה שחייבין עליה בחוץ:
Tosafot on Zevachim 4b:9:1.english: Since it is a rite, and they are liable - Explanation: a rite for which one is liable if performed outside [the Temple]:

Zevachim 4b:23:1.hebrew: אשכחן שלמים: בין בשינוי קודש בין בשינוי בעלים.
Zevachim 4b:23:1.english: We have found a source for peace offerings: both for deviation from the type of offering and for deviation regarding the owner.

Zevachim 4b:24.english: And if you would say: Let us derive from a peace offering that all offerings must be sacrificed with these intentions, this derivation can be refuted: What is unique about a peace offering? It is unique in that it requires laying hands on the head of the offering, and it is accompanied by libations, and the waving of the breast and the right hind leg by the priest and the owner; none of which is required for the firstborn offering.

Zevachim 4b:26:1.hebrew: אימא היכא דשחיט שלא לשמן ליפסלו: תימה, הא בכל דוכתא בעינן בקדשים שינה לעכב, והכא לא שינה? וי"ל דפריך משינוי קודש דאיכא תרי קראי ואמרי' לעיל: 'אם אינו ענין לשינוי קודש, תנהו ענין לשינוי בעלים', ופריך דהשתא אימר תרוייהו בשינוי קודש ולעכב? וקשה, מאי משני 'אמר קרא מוצא שפתיך'? דלמא ההוא קרא אתא לשינוי בעלים, דלא אשכחן ששינה בהן הכתוב, ולא קשה מידי דמוצא שפתיך לא משמע שינוי בעלים. ונראה דפריך מכח סברא כעין קושיא דר"ל דלקמיה ד'אימא דליפסלו', כיון דאמרת דלא עלו לשם חובה, או נימא דיעלו דאם כשרין הן ירצו ואם אין מרצין למה באין? לא דמי דריש לקיש פריך 'יהו כשרין גמורין' כמו שאר קדשים דלא שנה לעכב בו ליפסלו. והכא לא הוה ליה למיפרך 'שלא לשמה ליפסלו', אלא הוה ליה למימר 'וליתכשרו ויעלו לחובה' כשאר קדשים שלא שנה לעכב, כל כמה דאכתי לא ידע קרא דמוצא שפתיך. ואי פריך ליפסלו דנגמר מחטאת ופסח בהיקישא ד'זאת התורה' כדפרישית בסמוך, אי ב'מה מצינו' איכא למיפרך 'שכן כרת'. וא' בהקישא ד'זאת התורה', א"כ ליכתוב חדא או לחטאת גרידא או פסח גרידא. ואי נאמר דבכל דוכתא דמצרכינן 'שנה לעכב' היינו מהכא, מדכתיב 'מוצא שפתיך' וגו', א"כ אתי שפיר הא דפריך 'וליפסלו' וכו'.
Zevachim 4b:26:1.english: Let us say that if one slaughtered not for its sake, they are disqualified: It is astounding, for in every place regarding consecrated items, we require 'repeating [the law] to make it indispensable,' but here it is not repeated? And one can say that it is a refutation from 'deviation from the type of offering,' for there are two verses, and we said above: 'If it is not needed for deviation from the type of offering, apply it to deviation regarding the owner.' And he refutes, 'Now say both are for deviation from the type of offering and to make it indispensable?' And it is difficult: What is the answer 'the verse says, 'That which has gone out of your lips''? Perhaps that verse came for deviation regarding the owner, as we do not find that the verse repeated concerning it. And it is not difficult, as 'That which has gone out of your lips' does not imply deviation regarding the owner. And it seems that he refutes based on a logical argument, similar to Reish Lakish's question below, 'Let us say they are disqualified,' since you said they did not satisfy the obligation. Or let us say they do satisfy the obligation, for if they are fit, let them propitiate, and if they do not propitiate, why are they brought? This is not similar, for Reish Lakish refutes, 'Let them be completely fit' like other consecrated items, where it is not repeated to make it indispensable so that they are disqualified. And here, he should not have refuted 'not for its sake, they are disqualified,' but rather he should have said, 'Let them be fit and satisfy the obligation' like other consecrated items for which it is not repeated to make it indispensable, as long as he does not yet know the verse 'That which has gone out of your lips,' etc. And if he refutes, 'they are disqualified,' which is derived from a sin offering and a Paschal offering by the juxtaposition of 'This is the law,' as I explained nearby, if in 'what do we find' there is a refutation because 'it is liable to karet.' And one in the juxtaposition of 'This is the law,' if so, let it write one, either for a sin offering alone or a Paschal offering alone. And if we say that in every place where we require 'repeating to make it indispensable,' it is from here, from 'That which has gone out of your lips,' etc., then it is good that he refutes, 'and let them be disqualified,' etc.
